narrative_purpose: Make the physical inhibitor stack tangible: a hardened hydrophobic ash crust a seedling cannot pierce, water beading and running off, and an erosion rill ready to strip anything that establishes.
subject: A close view of a cracked, hardened grey ash crust on a gentle slope. A single small seedling wilts where its root failed to penetrate the crust. Beads of rainwater sit on the crust surface and trickle downhill rather than soaking in. A shallow erosion rill (a small gully) cuts down the slope nearby, carrying loose grey sediment.
scene: A barren ashland slope surface in close view, the cracked crust filling most of the frame, the rill cutting through one side.
camera: Close low oblique shot across the crust surface, following the slope downhill.
light: Dim flat overcast light; the wilting seedling carries only the faintest fading teal, emphasising failure; cool grey throughout.
palette: Uniform stone-grey crust and indigo shadow in the cracks, a weak fading teal on the dying seedling, no warm accent.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, bleak surface study.
detail_level: High detail on the cracked crust texture, the beading water and the failing seedling; slope softens into haze.
composition: Cracked crust across the frame, the seedling just off-centre, water beads catching light, the rill cutting one edge; leave a plain dim area for later callouts.
consistency_notes: Everything signals a hostile surface: sealed crust, water running off not soaking in, erosion, a failing seedling. No thriving vegetation anywhere. Cool grey Pandora palette. Keep open dark space for callouts.
